This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game studio. Then it explains one idea. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary open-asset asset-library licence creative-commons royalty-free attribution tasl credits-screen credits-file open-font-licence rights-clearance >}}

## 13.1 Where can assets come from?

- **Own work**, **open asset sites**, **paid libraries**, **public
  domain**, **freelancers**.
- Keep the proof: the licence page, the receipt, the contract.
- An image search is not a source.

![Where assets can come from.](images/asset-sources.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Download from the creator's page or a known library, not a re-upload.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find two assets"}
Find a sound and an image you may use in a game for sale; write the site
and the licence.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "A rain sound on an open sound site, CC BY 4.0,
by its author's page. A tree image on an art site, CC0." Both allow a game
for sale; the page of each is saved.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Sources and proofs"}
Choose the proof to keep.

::: {.match extra="a screenshot of a search|nothing"}
a sound from an open sound site
:   the saved licence page

    Why: The saved page shows the licence you agreed to.

music from a freelancer
:   the signed contract

    Why: The contract decides what the studio may do.

a sprite pack bought in a store
:   the receipt and the licence

    Why: The receipt and the licence prove the purchase.

art drawn by an employee
:   nothing extra (work for hire)

    Why: Work for hire belongs to the studio.
:::
:::

## 13.2 Read and save the licence

- Check the **author**, the **exact licence**, **commercial use** and
  **changes**, the **credit**, **other limits**.
- Save the page as a PDF with the date.

![Reading a licence page.](images/licence-page.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"Free" can mean free of cost, not free to use in a game for sale.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Read a licence page"}
Answer the five questions for one of your assets and save its page.

::: {.check}
A good answer gives the author (a person), the exact licence with its
version (CC BY 4.0), commercial use and changes (allowed or not), the
credit asked for, and other limits; the page is saved as a PDF with the
date.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Night Rain"}
Read the licence page. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the website|no"}
the author
:   Lina Haddad

    Why: The author is a person, not the website.

the licence
:   CC BY 4.0

    Why: The exact licence has its version: 4.0.

commercial use and changes
:   allowed

    Why: CC BY allows commercial use and changes.

selling the sound file alone
:   not allowed

    Why: Selling the file alone is a limit of the licence.
:::
:::

## 13.3 Credits with TASL

- **T**itle, **A**uthor, **S**ource, **L**icence (+ the changes).
- In the **credits screen** and the **credits file**.

![A credit with TASL.](images/tasl.png){width=94%}

![Credits screen and credits file.](images/credits.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/credit-builder.html" poster="sims/credit-builder.png" title="Credit Builder: TASL for Rooftop Rescue" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"Sounds from the Internet" is not a credit.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your credits file"}
In **Credit Builder**, build the three credits; start a credits file for
your two assets.

::: {.check}
Credit Builder: "Night Rain" by Lina Haddad, sounds.example.org, CC BY 4.0,
shortened to 20 s; "Roof Tiles Pack" by Karim Art, CC BY-SA 4.0,
recoloured by Nour; "Roof Sans" by Omar Studio, SIL OFL 1.1. Your file has
one TASL line for each of your two assets.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · TASL"}
Use Credit Builder. Choose the part of the credit.

::: {.match extra="the file size|the price"}
"Night Rain"
:   the title

    Why: T is the title of the work.

Lina Haddad
:   the author

    Why: A is the author.

sounds.example.org/night-rain
:   the source

    Why: S is the source: where the work is.

CC BY 4.0
:   the licence

    Why: L is the licence.
:::
:::

## 13.4 Check every asset before the release

- Five questions for each asset: **1** Who made it? **2** Who owns it?
  **3** Which licence? **4** Does our use fit? **5** Is the credit written?
- A status for each asset: **cleared** (all yes), **to fix** (a credit or
  a contract is missing), **replace** (unknown source, or the licence does
  not allow our use).
- Check the store page and the trailer too.

![A rights check.](../week-13/images/rights-check.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
An image search is not a source: an asset with an unknown source is
replaced.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Give a status"}
Give a status (cleared, to fix or replace) to four assets of your credits
file or of a game you imagine, with a reason for each.

::: {.check}
A good answer: "a sound under CC BY with its credit: cleared; music from a
freelancer without a contract: to fix (sign a contract); a photo from an
image search: replace; a font under OFL without a credit: to fix (write
the credit)." Each status has a reason.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The status"}
Choose the status.

::: {.match extra="sell it|hide it"}
A thunder sound, CC BY, with its credit written.
:   cleared

    Why: All five answers are yes.

Theme music by a freelancer, paid, but with no contract.
:   to fix: sign a contract

    Why: Without a contract, the freelancer still owns the music.

A cloud photo from an image search, page unknown.
:   replace

    Why: An unknown source cannot be cleared.

A font under the SIL Open Font License, no credit yet.
:   to fix: write the credit

    Why: The OFL needs a credit; it is missing.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Asset Shopping {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

Six assets: a **thunder sound** (CC BY), **cloud sprites** (CC0), a **cat
sprite** for non-commercial use, **roof tiles** (CC BY-SA) to recolour, a
**pixel font** (OFL) and **theme music** from a freelancer with a signed
contract.

{{< sim file="sims/asset-shopping.html" poster="sims/asset-shopping.png" title="Asset Shopping: six assets for a game for sale" kind="game" height="520" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The shopping list"}
Choose what Night Owl must do.

::: {.match extra="sell the file|hide the credit"}
the thunder sound, CC BY
:   use it with a TASL credit

    Why: CC BY needs a TASL credit.

the cat sprite, non-commercial only
:   do not use it in a game for sale

    Why: A game for sale is commercial use.

the recoloured roof tiles, CC BY-SA
:   share the changes under CC BY-SA

    Why: SA means share changes under the same licence.

the theme music, with a signed contract
:   use it with the credit of the contract

    Why: The signed contract gives the rights and names the credit.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Assets come from own work, open sites, paid libraries, the public domain
  and freelancers.
- Read the licence page and save it.
- Credit every asset with TASL in the credits screen and the credits file.
- Check every asset with five questions, and give it a status: cleared,
  to fix or replace.
- Keep every proof in the project.
